selected_evidence.summary: mkfs.xfs + mount succeeded; df -h showed /dev/mapper/datavg-datalv mounted at /srv/data.
vgextend + lvextend -L 2200M + xfs_growfs run against the still-mounted /srv/data; df -h confirmed 2.1G filesystem size and lvextend log shows resize from 1000MiB to <2.15GiB without unmounting.

selected_evidence.requirement: Contents stay intact through the grow
selected_evidence.summary: sha256 checksums of a text file and a 50MB random blob recorded before the grow and re-verified (OK) immediately after xfs_growfs completed.

selected_evidence.requirement: No spare disk existed; justification for loop-device-backed PVs
selected_evidence.summary: lsblk and parted free-space check showed the single 20GB disk fully partitioned with zero free space, ruling out adding a real second partition/disk as a PV.

selected_evidence.requirement: Boot-time persistence design and pre-reboot validation
selected_evidence.summary: systemd unit enabled, fstab entry added, and the generated srv-data.mount unit started directly (after manually detaching loops/VG) to prove the dependency chain reattaches loops, activates the VG, and remounts /srv/data with data intact — without requiring a real reboot.
Captured boot_id, service enablement, df -h, lvs sizing, and file checksums immediately before issuing the reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection (mandatory protocol)
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot command returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately; the very next exec call failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down shortly after acknowledgement.

selected_evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity and post-restart recovery proof (mandatory protocol) — NOT MET for node1
selected_evidence.summary: Repeated boot_id polls across ~48 minutes post-reboot all failed at the connection level (reset/timeout), never returning a boot_id. This is evidence of the limitation, not of recovery: node1's restart persistence and post-restart health cannot be confirmed, most likely because the /srv/data fstab entry (added without nofail) triggered an emergency-mode boot that requires console access unavailable through the exec tool.

commands.command:
sudo tee /usr/local/sbin/attach-lvm-loops.sh > /dev/null <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -e
for f in /var/lib/lvm-loop/disk1.img /var/lib/lvm-loop/disk2.img; do
  if ! losetup -j "$f" | grep -q .; then
    losetup -f "$f"
  fi
done
udevadm settle || true
vgchange -ay datavg || true
ANTRIEB_EOF
sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/attach-lvm-loops.sh
cat /usr/local/sbin/attach-lvm-loops.sh

[Unit]
Description=Attach loop devices and activate datavg for /srv/data
DefaultDependencies=no
After=systemd-udev-settle.service
Before=local-fs-pre.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/attach-lvm-loops.sh

[Install]
WantedBy=local-fs-pre.target
ANTRIEB_EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable loop-lvm-setup.service

grep -q datalv /etc/fstab || echo '/dev/datavg/datalv /srv/data xfs defaults,x-systemd.requires=loop-lvm-setup.service 0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
